p-h-root-0.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-root-0.title: Which 10th gen you have matters
p-h-root-0.body: The 2.0 NA and the 1.5T are completely different platforms to mod. Almost nothing on this tree applies to the base 2.0.

p-h-root-1.author: fk8envy
p-h-root-1.title: Trim comparison, LX vs Si
p-h-root-1.body: Side by side. The Si brake and wheel package is worth buying into up front rather than retrofitting.

p-h-root-2.author: boostleak
p-h-root-2.title: Buy the trim you actually want to end up with
p-h-root-2.body: Started on an LX planning to swap everything. Ended up selling it and buying an Si instead — cheaper in the end than chasing parity part by part.

p-h-root-3.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-root-3.title: Three trims side by side at a meet
p-h-root-3.body: LX, Si and a K24-swapped car parked together by accident. Good visual for how differently this platform splits.

p-h-15t-0.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-15t-0.title: FlashPro is the whole mod
p-h-15t-0.body: Stage 1 on 91 was worth about 40whp and 60lb-ft over stock. Nothing else on this list comes close per dollar.

p-h-15t-1.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-15t-1.title: 1.5T before and after the flash
p-h-15t-1.body: Transcript: two pulls, stock map then stage 1. The difference is mostly in how early it pulls rather than the top end.

p-h-15t-2.author: vtec_yo
p-h-15t-2.title: Watch your intake air temps
p-h-15t-2.body: Stock intercooler heat-soaks in about three pulls. The tune will pull timing and you will wonder where the power went.

p-h-15t-3.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-15t-3.title: Boost gauge added post-tune
p-h-15t-3.body: Cheap add, but knowing peak boost on every pull caught a leaking coupler before it became a real problem.

p-h-15t-4.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-15t-4.title: This is the mod that actually changes daily driving
p-h-15t-4.body: Everything after this on the tree is nice to have. The FlashPro is the one that changes how the car feels every single drive.

p-h-si-0.author: k20c2_si
p-h-si-0.title: Stock Si exhaust, for reference
p-h-si-0.body: Recording this before anything goes on the exhaust so there's a baseline to compare against. K20C2, stock everything from the turbo back. It is quiet — almost disappointingly so for what the engine actually is.

p-h-si-1.author: k20c2_si
p-h-si-1.title: The factory LSD changes everything
p-h-si-1.body: Coming from the 1.5T, the Si putting power down out of a corner is the real upgrade. The extra 25hp is almost incidental.

p-h-si-2.author: fk8envy
p-h-si-2.title: 25psi on the stock K20C2
p-h-si-2.body: Boost log screenshot. Held flat to redline once the intercooler was sorted.

p-h-si-3.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-si-3.title: Si next to the 1.5T it replaced
p-h-si-3.body: Traded a tuned 1.5T for this stock Si and I'm still not sure I made the right call. Ask me again once the exhaust goes on.

p-h-si-4.author: torque_curve
p-h-si-4.title: The LSD alone is worth cross-shopping used
p-h-si-4.body: Found a clean used Si for barely more than a tuned 1.5T would've cost. If you can find one, the diff changes the math on the whole build.

p-h-k24-0.author: itb_addict
p-h-k24-0.title: K24 with ITBs at 8000rpm
p-h-k24-0.body: Transcript: individual throttle bodies on an NA K24. The induction noise above 6000 is the entire reason people do this swap.

p-h-k24-1.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-k24-1.title: ITB linkage clearance
p-h-k24-1.body: Sketch of where the linkage fouls the strut tower on an FC. Needs a spacer or a shortened arm.

p-h-k24-2.author: vtec_yo
p-h-k24-2.title: Swap cost reality check
p-h-k24-2.body: Motor, mounts, harness, ECU and tune came to about $8,500 done properly. A tuned Si is faster for half that.

p-h-k24-3.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-k24-3.title: Cold start, idle only
p-h-k24-3.body: Recorded before any driving, just letting the ITBs settle at idle. That slight lope is the cams, not a tuning issue — took me a week to stop worrying about it.

p-h-k24-4.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-k24-4.title: ITB linkage after the fix
p-h-k24-4.body: Shortened arm cleared the strut tower with about 4mm to spare. Ugly fix, works perfectly.

p-h-k24-5.author: civic_daily
p-h-k24-5.title: Nobody does this swap for the numbers
p-h-k24-5.body: Objectively worse power-to-dollar than either turbo option. Do it because you want an NA Honda that revs to 8500, not because it's efficient.

p-h-15t-quiet-0.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-15t-quiet-0.title: The 1.5T drone is real
p-h-15t-quiet-0.body: Any non-resonated catback on the 1.5T booms at 2200rpm, which is exactly highway cruise. Do not skip the resonator on this engine.

p-h-15t-quiet-1.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-15t-quiet-1.title: Resonator position
p-h-15t-quiet-1.body: Where the second resonator sits. This position was quiet; 300mm forward was not.

p-h-15t-quiet-2.author: itb_addict
p-h-15t-quiet-2.title: Highway drone gone completely after the resonator
p-h-15t-quiet-2.body: Went from genuinely annoying to not noticing the exhaust exists on a 3-hour drive. Should've done this on install day one.

p-h-15t-quiet-3.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-15t-quiet-3.title: Underside shot showing both resonators
p-h-15t-quiet-3.body: Two in series, not one bigger one. This is what actually kills the 1.5T drone.

p-h-si-3in-0.author: k20c2_si
p-h-si-3in-0.title: Check this out — 3in turbo-back on
p-h-si-3in-0.body: Same car, same road, same gear as the clip up on the Si node. Downpipe and catback both done. Turn it up. You can finally hear the turbo doing something instead of the muffler eating all of it.

p-h-si-3in-1.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-si-3in-1.title: Downpipe is worth more than the catback
p-h-si-3in-1.body: Most of the gain was the downpipe. The catback was mostly noise — worth doing in that order if you are spreading the cost.

p-h-si-3in-2.author: k20c2_si
p-h-si-3in-2.title: Si turbo-back, third gear pull
p-h-si-3in-2.body: Transcript: full pull in third with the 3in system. Turbo spool is audible over the exhaust, which it was not with the stock downpipe.

p-h-si-3in-3.author: itb_addict
p-h-si-3in-3.title: Downpipe on the bench before install
p-h-si-3in-3.body: 3in catted, ceramic coated. Coating alone was worth it after seeing how the uncoated test pipe discolored.

p-h-si-3in-4.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-si-3in-4.title: This exhaust turned heads at a gas station for the first time
p-h-si-3in-4.body: Never happened on the stock system. People assumed it was already an Si with how it sounded, now they can hear it too.

p-h-k24-header-0.author: torque_curve
p-h-k24-header-0.title: Nothing happens below 5000
p-h-k24-header-0.body: The 4-1 moved the whole powerband up. Great on track, genuinely worse in traffic than stock.

p-h-k24-header-1.author: k20c2_si
p-h-k24-header-1.title: Header clearance to the rack
p-h-k24-header-1.body: Tight but no contact. Photo taken with the engine at full load lean.

p-h-k24-header-2.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-k24-header-2.title: Traffic is genuinely worse now, and I'd still do it again
p-h-k24-header-2.body: Nothing below 5000 is not an exaggeration. Stop-and-go commute is worse than stock. Sound and top end are worth it to me anyway.

p-h-k24-header-3.author: itb_addict
p-h-k24-header-3.title: Header ceramic coat after a season
p-h-k24-header-3.body: Zero discoloration after a full summer of heat cycles. Worth the extra cost on a header that runs this hot.

p-h-15t-18-0.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-15t-18-0.title: 18s ride worse than you expect
p-h-15t-18-0.body: Going from 17 to 18 on a 40-series noticeably firmed up the ride on bad roads. Worth it visually, not mechanically.

p-h-15t-18-1.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-15t-18-1.title: 235/40 fitment, no spacers
p-h-15t-18-1.body: Sits flush with the arch. No rubbing at full lock or over speed bumps.

p-h-15t-18-2.author: fk8envy
p-h-15t-18-2.title: Went back to 17s after a season on 18s
p-h-15t-18-2.body: Wanted the look, but potholes on my commute made me regret it within six months. Traded back down and don't miss it.

p-h-15t-18-3.author: itb_addict
p-h-15t-18-3.title: 18s next to the stock 16s
p-h-15t-18-3.body: Size difference is bigger in person than in photos. Fills the arch completely at this offset.

p-h-si-track-0.author: k20c2_si
p-h-si-track-0.title: 200TW is the sweet spot for street-track
p-h-si-track-0.body: Full R-comps were faster but useless in rain and lasted four events. 200TW does most of it and survives the drive home.

p-h-si-track-2.author: civic_daily
p-h-si-track-2.title: 200TW held up for two full seasons
p-h-si-track-2.body: Longer than I expected honestly. Rotate them and you'll get real mileage even tracking semi-regularly.

p-h-si-track-3.author: itb_addict
p-h-si-track-3.title: Track day, first session on the new wheels

p-h-k24-light-0.author: itb_addict
p-h-k24-light-0.title: 17s keep the gearing alive
p-h-k24-light-0.body: The NA K24 does not have the torque to pull tall gearing. Going down to 17s made it feel considerably quicker without changing power.

p-h-k24-light-1.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-k24-light-1.title: Offset comparison sketch
p-h-k24-light-1.body: What +45 versus +35 does to the arch gap on an FC.

p-h-k24-light-2.author: itb_addict
p-h-k24-light-2.title: 17s at ride height on the K24 car
p-h-k24-light-2.body: Smaller diameter, more sidewall. Rides noticeably better than the 18s did on the same suspension.

p-h-k24-light-3.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-k24-light-3.title: Gearing math actually checks out
p-h-k24-light-3.body: Did the calculation before buying — effective final drive works out close enough to stock that acceleration feel barely changed despite the smaller wheel.

p-h-15t-street-0.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-15t-street-0.title: This is the one to copy
p-h-15t-street-0.body: Quiet, quick, comfortable, passes inspection. If you want one build off this whole tree, it is this one.

p-h-15t-street-1.author: boostleak
p-h-15t-street-1.title: Pad dust warning
p-h-15t-street-1.body: The street performance pads dust heavily on light wheels. Budget for cleaning them weekly or go to a low-dust compound.

p-h-15t-street-2.author: boostleak
p-h-15t-street-2.title: Finished daily, a year on
p-h-15t-street-2.body: Nothing changed since this build finished. That's the whole point — it does everything I need and I stopped tinkering.

p-h-15t-street-3.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-15t-street-3.title: Recommend this build to anyone asking where to start
p-h-15t-street-3.body: Quiet, quick, reliable. If someone shows me this tree and asks what to build first, it's this one every time.

p-h-si-bbk-0.author: itb_addict
p-h-si-bbk-0.title: The Si's real weak point
p-h-si-bbk-0.body: Stock Si brakes fade on lap three of any real session. The 330mm setup held for a full 20-minute run without a wobble.

p-h-si-bbk-2.author: itb_addict
p-h-si-bbk-2.title: Two-piece rotors are worth it here
p-h-si-bbk-2.body: Cracked a one-piece within two events. The two-piece has done a season.

p-h-si-bbk-3.author: fk8envy
p-h-si-bbk-3.title: Rotor and pad after a track weekend
p-h-si-bbk-3.body: Even wear across both. No cracking, no glazing. Worth every bit of the upfront cost.

p-h-si-bbk-4.author: vtec_yo
p-h-si-bbk-4.title: Pedal feel took a session to get used to
p-h-si-bbk-4.body: Bite point moved noticeably closer to the floor compared to stock. Felt wrong for one session, then became normal.

p-h-hybrid-0.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-hybrid-0.title: Why NA on a chassis built for boost
p-h-hybrid-0.body: Throttle response. The K24 gives up 60hp to the tuned Si but does exactly what your right foot asks, instantly.

p-h-hybrid-1.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-hybrid-1.title: K24 in the Si chassis, first drive
p-h-hybrid-1.body: Transcript: first proper drive after the swap. You can hear the ITBs over the exhaust at part throttle, which never happened in the FC shell.

p-h-hybrid-2.author: civic_daily
p-h-hybrid-2.title: The brakes are overkill now
p-h-hybrid-2.body: 330mm on a car that lost 80kg of turbo plumbing. Not complaining, but you could run a smaller setup and save weight.

p-h-hybrid-3.author: civic_daily
p-h-hybrid-3.title: Finished build, first proper photo
p-h-hybrid-3.body: Every part on this car came from somewhere else on this tree. Feels less like a build and more like an argument I finally won.

p-h-hybrid-4.author: k20c2_si
p-h-hybrid-4.title: This is the one everyone asks about at meets
p-h-hybrid-4.body: Nobody expects the NA engine note out of what looks like a boosted Si. Explaining it takes longer than showing them.

p-h-typer-0.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-typer-0.title: Why a full engine, not just a head swap
p-h-typer-0.body: Trans comes with it either way, so keep the ECU and diff and skip the adapter-plate compromises. Total swap kit ran $9,400 including tax on the donor engine.

p-h-typer-1.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-typer-1.title: Donor engine on the stand
p-h-typer-1.body: FK8 had 11k miles. Should've been an easy sell for someone, but insurance wrote the whole car off for a bent subframe.

p-h-typer-2.author: itb_addict
p-h-typer-2.title: Wiring is the actual project
p-h-typer-2.body: Bolting the motor in took a weekend. Getting the FK8 harness talking to an FC dash took three.

p-h-typer-3.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-typer-3.title: First start after the swap
p-h-typer-3.body: Transcript: cranks for a beat longer than expected, then catches. Idle settles fast — whatever they retuned about idle control on the Type R is noticeably smoother than the old 1.5T.

p-h-typer-4.author: civic_daily
p-h-typer-4.title: Cold start, first drive around the block

p-h-typer-5.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-typer-5.title: Still not registered and I don't care
p-h-typer-5.body: Paperwork on a swapped VIN is its own project. Drove it around the neighborhood anyway. Worth it.

p-h-typer-hks-0.author: civic_daily
p-h-typer-hks-0.title: Keeping the OEM downpipe was the right call
p-h-typer-hks-0.body: HKS catback bolts straight to the factory turbo-back. No fabrication, no rubbing on the crossmember.

p-h-typer-hks-1.author: torque_curve
p-h-typer-hks-1.title: Legamax fitment at the rear
p-h-typer-hks-1.body: Tucks tighter than the OEM FK8 tips did. No trimming needed on this bumper.

p-h-typer-hks-2.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-typer-hks-2.title: Quieter than I expected for the badge
p-h-typer-hks-2.body: Legamax at idle is almost civil. It's the mid-range where it actually opens up.

p-h-typer-hks-3.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-typer-hks-3.title: Cabin note at 4000rpm
p-h-typer-hks-3.body: Transcript: pull in third gear, windows up. Drone is minimal for a straight swap onto a smaller chassis than it was designed for.

p-h-typer-19-0.author: itb_addict
p-h-typer-19-0.title: Bolt pattern matches, offset does not quite
p-h-typer-19-0.body: 5x114.3 carries over but you're running about 3mm more poke than stock FK8 fitment on this chassis. Fine on the street, watch it on speed bumps.

p-h-typer-19-1.author: flashpro_fc
p-h-typer-19-1.title: 19s tucked at ride height
p-h-typer-19-1.body: No spacers. Slight lip rub at full compression, otherwise clean.

p-h-typer-19-2.author: torque_curve
p-h-typer-19-2.title: Weight penalty nobody mentions
p-h-typer-19-2.body: OEM Type R wheels are not light. Went up almost a kilo a corner over the forged 18s on the Si tree.

p-h-typer-brembo-0.author: torque_curve
p-h-typer-brembo-0.title: Direct fit, genuinely no adapter needed
p-h-typer-brembo-0.body: Same bolt pattern as the FC subframe. Ten minutes longer than a pad swap once the calipers were on the bench.

p-h-typer-brembo-1.author: boostleak
p-h-typer-brembo-1.title: Brembo calipers before paint
p-h-typer-brembo-1.body: Left them factory red. Wanted the FK8 badge to actually mean something under the wheel.

p-h-typer-brembo-2.author: itb_addict
p-h-typer-brembo-2.title: This is the build to copy if you have the budget
p-h-typer-brembo-2.body: Type R everything under an FC shell that still looks stock in traffic. Best of both.

p-h-typer-brembo-3.author: swapped_not_stock
p-h-typer-brembo-3.title: First track day on the finished build

p-h-typer-brembo-4.author: itb_addict
p-h-typer-brembo-4.title: Damn, this thing finally exists
p-h-typer-brembo-4.body: Eighteen months from the first parts bin to a finished car. Sat in the driveway for ten minutes just looking at it before I even opened the door.

p-c-root-0.author: rallybrain
p-c-root-0.title: Why start here
p-c-root-0.body: Every build on this page grew from a bone-stock 1.8L. Worth knowing the baseline is 132hp before you read anyone's dyno claim.

p-c-root-1.author: dailydriven_e170
p-c-root-1.title: Stock engine bay, 2016
p-c-root-1.body: Reference shot before anything was touched. Useful for spotting what has actually changed in the photos further down the tree.

p-c-root-2.author: dailydriven_e170
p-c-root-2.title: The car that started this page
p-c-root-2.body: Bought it for $4,200 with 140k on the clock because it was the only manual left in the classifieds. Everything below traces back to this exact car.

p-c-root-3.author: rallybrain
p-c-root-3.title: The 2ZR block is tougher than people give it credit for
p-c-root-3.body: 140k miles before anyone touched the head. Whatever else you hear about these, the bottom end holds up.

p-c-na-0.author: rallybrain
p-c-na-0.title: Header routing diagram
p-c-na-0.body: Blueprint of the 4-2-1 primaries and where they clear the steering shaft. Useful if you are fabricating rather than buying.

p-c-na-1.author: gravelspec
p-c-na-1.title: Tune before you spend on hardware
p-c-na-1.body: The intake alone did almost nothing measurable. Same intake with a proper tune was worth about 14whp. Order matters more than parts here.

p-c-na-2.author: nine_psi
p-c-na-2.title: Header fitment on a 2016
p-c-na-2.body: The 4-2-1 fouls the OEM heat shield. Ten minutes with tin snips or you will hear it rattling at every light.

p-c-na-3.author: wrenchmonkey
p-c-na-3.title: Finished bay, four months in
p-c-na-3.body: Every bracket that could be cleaned up, was. Still just an NA 1.8 underneath, but it doesn't look like it anymore.

p-c-na-4.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-na-4.title: Ceramic coat the header or regret it
p-c-na-4.body: Uncoated one on mine discolored within a month. The coated header two builds later still looks new.

p-c-na-5.author: wrenchmonkey
p-c-na-5.title: This is still the build I recommend first
p-c-na-5.body: Cheapest entry, least that can go wrong, and it is still noticeably quicker than stock. Start here before you talk yourself into a turbo.

p-c-turbo-0.author: nine_psi
p-c-turbo-0.title: Corolla revving — 8psi spool
p-c-turbo-0.body: Cold start then three pulls to redline. Spool comes in around 3200 and you can hear the blow-off between shifts. No rattle on overrun, so the wastegate is holding.

p-c-turbo-1.author: torque_curve
p-c-turbo-1.title: Boost ceiling on a stock block
p-c-turbo-1.body: 8psi has held for 20k miles on mine. Everyone I know who pushed past 10 on a stock bottom end lost ringlands within a season.

p-c-turbo-2.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-turbo-2.title: Intercooler piping routing
p-c-turbo-2.body: Piping runs behind the bumper support rather than through it — no cutting, and it comes out again in twenty minutes.

p-c-turbo-3.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-turbo-3.title: Stock baseline before the downpipe
p-c-turbo-3.body: Recording this before the 3in setup goes on so there is an actual before-and-after instead of just claims. GT2860 at 8psi, stock downpipe and catback, everything else untouched.

p-c-turbo-4.author: gravelspec
p-c-turbo-4.title: Engine bay after the intercooler swap
p-c-turbo-4.body: Front-mount replaced the side-mount from the kit. Charge pipe routing got a lot simpler.

p-c-turbo-5.author: rallybrain
p-c-turbo-5.title: Fuel is the part people forget to budget
p-c-turbo-5.body: Stock injectors held to about 9psi on my car before the logs showed lean spikes. Budget for injectors if you are pushing past 8.

p-c-built-0.author: torque_curve
p-c-built-0.title: What forged actually costs
p-c-built-0.body: Rods, pistons, bearings, machining and gaskets came to about $3,400 before labour. The turbo was the cheap part of this step.

p-c-built-1.author: rallybrain
p-c-built-1.title: Bearing clearance notes
p-c-built-1.body: Sketch of the clearances we ended up at after machining. Slightly loose on the mains for the boost target.

p-c-built-2.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-built-2.title: Block on the bench before assembly
p-c-built-2.body: Bored 0.5mm over, forged rods and pistons staged next to it. This is the point of no return on cost.

p-c-built-3.author: nine_psi
p-c-built-3.title: Machine shop choice matters more than parts choice
p-c-built-3.body: Went with a shop that specializes in these blocks specifically. Clearances came back tighter than a generalist shop quoted.

p-c-na-quiet-0.author: dailydriven_e170
p-c-na-quiet-0.title: Resonator placement matters
p-c-na-quiet-0.body: First catback droned badly at 70mph. Moving the resonator 200mm further back killed it completely. Same pipe, same muffler.

p-c-na-quiet-1.author: gravelspec
p-c-na-quiet-1.title: Tip alignment after the swap
p-c-na-quiet-1.body: Tips sit 8mm proud of the bumper cut. Looks intentional rather than like something fell off.

p-c-na-quiet-2.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-na-quiet-2.title: Resonator brand actually makes a difference here
p-c-na-quiet-2.body: Tried two before landing on one that killed the drone without choking flow. The cheapest option made it worse, not better.

p-c-na-quiet-3.author: dailydriven_e170
p-c-na-quiet-3.title: Muffler shop welds, close up
p-c-na-quiet-3.body: Paid the extra $40 for someone who does this daily instead of a general shop. Seams are half the thickness of my last car's.

p-c-turbo-3in-0.author: torque_curve
p-c-turbo-3in-0.title: Downpipe clearance sketch
p-c-turbo-3in-0.body: Where the 3in downpipe fouls the steering rack. Needs a dimple or you will feel it through the wheel at idle.

p-c-turbo-3in-1.author: gravelspec
p-c-turbo-3in-1.title: Catless on a daily
p-c-turbo-3in-1.body: Fine until inspection. If your state tests, budget for a high-flow cat now rather than redoing the whole mid-pipe later.

p-c-turbo-3in-2.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-turbo-3in-2.title: Same car, downpipe and catback both on now
p-c-turbo-3in-2.body: Same road, same gear as the stock clip up on the Turbo node. Turn it up — you can actually hear the wastegate now instead of it getting swallowed by the stock system.

p-c-turbo-3in-3.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-turbo-3in-3.title: Downpipe alone was most of the sound change
p-c-turbo-3in-3.body: Catback added maybe 10% more on top of that. If you are doing this in stages, the downpipe is the one that actually changes the character.

p-c-built-straight-0.author: e170_owner
p-c-built-straight-0.title: Corolla revving — big turbo, 18psi
p-c-built-straight-0.body: Transcript: much later spool than the GT2860, nothing until about 4000rpm, then it comes in hard. Straight-through is loud enough that the intake noise disappears above 5000.

p-c-built-straight-1.author: slowcarfast
p-c-built-straight-1.title: Not road legal, and not pleasant
p-c-built-straight-1.body: Drone between 2500 and 3000 is genuinely painful on a highway. This is a trailer-it-to-the-track setup.

p-c-built-straight-2.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-built-straight-2.title: Turbo-back laid out before install
p-c-built-straight-2.body: 3.5in mandrel bent, no resonator, no muffler. This is what 'not road legal' actually looks like in parts form.

p-c-built-straight-3.author: rallybrain
p-c-built-straight-3.title: Wear earplugs, seriously
p-c-built-straight-3.body: Did a two-hour track day without them once. Ears rang the whole drive home. Learn from me.

p-c-built-clearance-0.author: gravelspec
p-c-built-clearance-0.title: Routing over the rear subframe
p-c-built-clearance-0.body: Photo of the high-clearance section. Roughly 90mm higher than the stock path at its lowest point.

p-c-built-clearance-1.author: wrenchmonkey
p-c-built-clearance-1.title: Heat shielding is not optional
p-c-built-clearance-1.body: Routing it that high puts the pipe near the fuel line. Wrap it or move the line — do not skip this.

p-c-built-clearance-2.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-built-clearance-2.title: Ground clearance number, measured
p-c-built-clearance-2.body: About 90mm more than the street routing at the lowest point. Cleared every rut on the stage roads I tested it on.

p-c-built-clearance-3.author: rallybrain
p-c-built-clearance-3.title: Skid plate added after the first rock strike
p-c-built-clearance-3.body: First stage put a dent straight into the pipe. Skid plate ever since, zero issues.

p-c-turbo-street-0.author: dailydriven_e170
p-c-turbo-street-0.title: 215/45 on a 17 is the sweet spot
p-c-turbo-street-0.body: Wider looked better but tramlined badly on grooved highway. Went back to 215 and the car is much calmer.

p-c-turbo-street-1.author: rallybrain
p-c-turbo-street-1.title: Fitment at stock height
p-c-turbo-street-1.body: No rubbing, no spacers. Roughly a finger of gap at the front arch.

p-c-turbo-street-2.author: slowcarfast
p-c-turbo-street-2.title: Ride height matters more than the wheel choice
p-c-turbo-street-2.body: Dropped 20mm and the 17s finally looked proportional. Stock height with these wheels looked off to me.

p-c-turbo-street-3.author: torque_curve
p-c-turbo-street-3.title: One year later, still on the same set
p-c-turbo-street-3.body: No curb rash, no bent barrels. These have survived a daily commute better than I expected.

p-c-built-track-0.author: e170_owner
p-c-built-track-0.title: Semi-slicks need heat
p-c-built-track-0.body: First two laps on cold R-comps are genuinely worse than the street tyre. Do not judge them on an out-lap.

p-c-built-track-1.author: slowcarfast
p-c-built-track-1.title: Wheel weight comparison
p-c-built-track-1.body: Forged 17s next to the stock 16s on a scale — 3.1kg lighter per corner.

p-c-built-track-2.author: nine_psi
p-c-built-track-2.title: Alignment specs that actually worked
p-c-built-track-2.body: -2.5 front camber, stock toe. Anything more aggressive just chewed the inside edge faster without a lap time gain I could measure.

p-c-built-gravel-0.author: rallybrain
p-c-built-gravel-0.title: Cheapest way to real sidewall
p-c-built-gravel-0.body: 215/65 on a 16in steel is the cheapest sidewall on this chassis. Whole setup under $600 used, and steels bend instead of cracking.

p-c-built-gravel-1.author: torque_curve
p-c-built-gravel-1.title: Spacer fitment at full lock
p-c-built-gravel-1.body: +30mm spacers, no rubbing at full lock after rolling the front lip. Photo is at full steering deflection.

p-c-built-gravel-2.author: e170_owner
p-c-built-gravel-2.title: Steel wheels bend instead of cracking, exactly as advertised
p-c-built-gravel-2.body: Curbed one hard on a rally stage. Popped back with a hammer instead of needing a whole new wheel. Would have been a DNF on the forged set.

p-c-built-gravel-3.author: nine_psi
p-c-built-gravel-3.title: Full set after a season of stages
p-c-built-gravel-3.body: Dents everywhere but none of them cracked. This is what 'cheap sidewall' actually buys you.

p-c-turbo-daily-0.author: nine_psi
p-c-turbo-daily-0.title: Stainless lines are the cheap win
p-c-turbo-daily-0.body: Pedal feel changed more from $60 of lines than from the pads. Do lines first if you are on a budget.

p-c-turbo-daily-1.author: wrenchmonkey
p-c-turbo-daily-1.title: Exhaust note at cruise
p-c-turbo-daily-1.body: Transcript: 70mph highway pull with the window down. Almost no drone — this is the resonated setup doing its job.

p-c-turbo-daily-2.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-turbo-daily-2.title: Finished daily, two years in
p-c-turbo-daily-2.body: Nothing left on the list. Every part on this build has a reason, and it still passes inspection every year without issue.

p-c-turbo-daily-3.author: rallybrain
p-c-turbo-daily-3.title: This is the one I point people to
p-c-turbo-daily-3.body: Newcomers always ask which build to copy. It's this one — quick enough to be fun, boring enough to not think about.

p-c-track-weapon-0.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-track-weapon-0.title: Pad choice over caliper size
p-c-track-weapon-0.body: The 4-pots looked great but the real change was going to a proper track pad. Stock calipers with good pads would have got 80% of this.

p-c-track-weapon-2.author: gravelspec
p-c-track-weapon-2.title: Rotor wear after a full season
p-c-track-weapon-2.body: Even wear, no cracking, no warping. The 320mm setup is doing exactly what it is supposed to.

p-c-track-weapon-3.author: rallybrain
p-c-track-weapon-3.title: Bleeding these properly takes two people
p-c-track-weapon-3.body: Long lines to the front means air pockets are easy to miss solo. Get a second set of hands or a pressure bleeder.

p-c-gravel-rally-0.author: wrenchmonkey
p-c-gravel-rally-0.title: Handbrake feel after the swap
p-c-gravel-rally-0.body: Transcript: walking through the hydraulic handbrake install and how much lever travel there is before it bites. Much shorter throw than the cable setup.

p-c-gravel-rally-1.author: boosted_2zr
p-c-gravel-rally-1.title: Rally pads are terrible cold
p-c-gravel-rally-1.body: Almost no bite for the first minute. Fine on a stage, genuinely dangerous on a school run.

p-c-gravel-rally-2.author: dailydriven_e170
p-c-gravel-rally-2.title: Handbrake lever, after the swap
p-c-gravel-rally-2.body: Shorter throw than stock, mounted about 20mm further back to clear the seat in a full-lock pull.

p-c-gravel-rally-3.author: rallybrain
p-c-gravel-rally-3.title: Warm the pads before you need them
p-c-gravel-rally-3.body: Learned this the hard way pulling the handbrake cold into a hairpin. Do a couple of test pulls before the stage starts.

p-c-rally-0.author: rallybrain
p-c-rally-0.title: Why 14psi instead of 18
p-c-rally-0.body: Dropped from 18 to 14 for gravel. Losing about 40hp, but heat soak on a long stage was killing it and I would rather finish.

p-c-rally-1.author: rallybrain
p-c-rally-1.title: Gravel test run — second gear pulls

p-c-rally-2.author: torque_curve
p-c-rally-2.title: The fusion actually works
p-c-rally-2.body: Track brakes on gravel wheels sounds wrong but the 4-pots cope with the heat far better than the vented discs did.

p-c-rally-3.author: e170_owner
p-c-rally-3.title: Finished rally build, morning of the first event
p-c-rally-3.body: Two years of parts sitting in a garage and it is finally a running, entered car. Still cannot quite believe it.

p-c-rally-4.author: gravelspec
p-c-rally-4.title: This is what the whole tree was building toward
p-c-rally-4.body: Every branch above fed into this one decision or another. Feels less like a build now and more like a conclusion.

p-w-root-0.author: boxer_rumble
p-w-root-0.title: The VA is the best value chassis here
p-w-root-0.body: AWD, a real gearbox and a factory turbo. Everything on this tree is cheaper than getting a FWD car to the same place.

p-w-root-1.author: va_commuter
p-w-root-1.title: Stock VA before anything
p-w-root-1.body: Baseline photo. Useful for spotting ride height changes further down.

p-w-stage1-0.author: stage_car_sam
p-w-stage1-0.title: Stock VA, before anything
p-w-stage1-0.body: Baseline recording. Stage 1 map, everything else factory. That boxer offbeat is there but the stock muffler is doing its job a bit too well. Posting it so the turbo-back clip further down has something to sit against.

p-w-stage1-1.author: stage_car_sam
p-w-stage1-1.title: OTS maps are genuinely safe here
p-w-stage1-1.body: Cobb's stage 1 has been run on thousands of these. If you are nervous about tuning, this is the one to start on.

p-w-stage1-2.author: stage_car_sam
p-w-stage1-2.title: Gains are modest but free-feeling
p-w-stage1-2.body: About 25whp. What you actually notice is the throttle response and how much earlier boost arrives.

p-w-stage2-0.author: boxer_rumble
p-w-stage2-0.title: Protune, not an OTS map
p-w-stage2-0.body: Stage 2 on an off-the-shelf map with a bigger intercooler ran lean at the top. Pay for the protune, it is $500 well spent.

p-w-stage2-1.author: awd_bias
p-w-stage2-1.title: TMIC versus the stock unit
p-w-stage2-1.body: Size comparison. Intake temps dropped about 18°C on a hot lap.

p-w-bigturbo-0.author: e85_only
p-w-bigturbo-0.title: E85 availability decides this build
p-w-bigturbo-0.body: The whole tune depends on E85. If your area does not have it reliably, this build becomes a very expensive stage 2.

p-w-bigturbo-1.author: e85_only
p-w-bigturbo-1.title: VF52 spool on E85
p-w-bigturbo-1.body: Transcript: cold start then a pull. Spool is noticeably later than the stock turbo but the top end keeps going where stage 2 flattens.

p-w-bigturbo-2.author: fa20_stage2
p-w-bigturbo-2.title: Rod bearings are the known failure
p-w-bigturbo-2.body: Built short block is not optional at this power. The FA20 drops bearings on stock rods surprisingly reliably above 400whp.

p-w-stage1-quiet-0.author: va_commuter
p-w-stage1-quiet-0.title: Keep the stock downpipe
p-w-stage1-quiet-0.body: The catback alone with the stock downpipe is the quietest way to get the boxer sound. Any downpipe change makes it drone.

p-w-stage1-quiet-1.author: rodbearing
p-w-stage1-quiet-1.title: Cabin noise at 75mph
p-w-stage1-quiet-1.body: Transcript: highway cruise recording. Conversation-level — this is a setup you can road trip in.

p-w-stage2-tb-0.author: fa20_stage2
p-w-stage2-tb-0.title: The map assumes the downpipe
p-w-stage2-tb-0.body: Do not run a stage 2 map on a stock downpipe. It will knock, and the logs will show it immediately.

p-w-stage2-tb-1.author: stage_car_sam
p-w-stage2-tb-1.title: Turbo-back on — listen to this
p-w-stage2-tb-1.body: Same stretch of road, same gear, right after the downpipe and catback went on. Compare it to the stock clip up on the Stage 1 node. This is what everyone means when they say the downpipe is the mod that matters.

p-w-stage2-tb-2.author: fa20_stage2
p-w-stage2-tb-2.title: Catted downpipe fitment
p-w-stage2-tb-2.body: Photo of the catted section. Passes inspection and only costs about 5whp against catless.

p-w-big-open-0.author: boxer_rumble
p-w-big-open-0.title: Genuinely antisocial
p-w-big-open-0.body: Catless and straight through on a boxer is loud in a way that gets you noticed by the wrong people. Fine for a stage car.

p-w-big-open-1.author: fa20_stage2
p-w-big-open-1.title: Downpipe routing sketch
p-w-big-open-1.body: Where the 3.5in sits relative to the steering shaft. Tight, needs wrapping.

p-w-stage1-oem-0.author: va_commuter
p-w-stage1-oem-0.title: Stock look, much better grip
p-w-stage1-oem-0.body: Same size as OEM so nothing rubs, but a proper summer tyre transformed the car more than the tune did.

p-w-stage2-track-0.author: fa20_stage2
p-w-stage2-track-0.title: Smaller wheel, more tyre
